images.title: 6 kg 40 g in grams
images.purpose: Show that the g part of a mixed weight takes three places: 6 kg is 6,000 g and 40 g is 040, so 6 kg 40 g is 6,040 g.
images.composition: The weight at the top, a kg box and a g box with three digit cells below it, the working in a bracket, and the result in grams.
images.exact_structure: Plain white frame, 1456 by 816. TITLE at the top centre, y 90: the text 6 kg 40 g (72 px, bold, dark #1F2937). SPLIT: two boxes side by side below the title. Box 1, centred at x 480, y 200 to 380, a rounded rectangle 280 by 180 px filled pale teal #CCE5F2 with a 4 px outline #0072B2, holding the number 6 (96 px, bold) with the small word kg (36 px) under it. Box 2, centred at x 976, y 200 to 380, a rounded rectangle 560 by 180 px filled pale amber #FBE7C0 with a 4 px outline #E69F00, holding THREE equal digit cells each 150 by 120 px with a 3 px dark outline, at x 700 to 850, 850 to 1000 and 1000 to 1150, containing the digits 0, 4 and 0 (80 px, bold), with the small word g (36 px) under the cells and the small words hundreds, tens and ones (28 px, grey #6B7280) above the three cells. A thin dark 3 px bracket under both boxes at y 420 from x 340 to x 1256 with the text 6 kg is 6 × 1,000 = 6,000 g centred at x 798, y 470 (40 px, dark). RESULT: centred at x 728, y 640, the text 6,040 g (96 px, bold, teal #0072B2) inside a rounded rectangle 560 by 120 px with a 4 px outline #0072B2, with a short thick arrow 60 px long from the bracket text down to it. SLIP NOTE at the bottom right, x 960 to 1420, y 720 to 790, a rounded rectangle with a 3 px outline #6B7280 and the text 6,400 g is 6 kg 400 g (32 px, dark), with a small cross mark (amber #E69F00, 36 px) at its left end. Nothing else in the frame.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
any count of digit cells that differs from 3 in the g box
the digits in the g box in any order other than 0, 4, 0
a result other than 6,040 g in the large box
images.takeaway: The g part of a mixed weight takes three places, so 6 kg 40 g is 6,040 g, not 6,400 g.
images.description: 6 kg 40 g split into a kg box and a g box of three digit cells, giving 6,040 g.
images.context: Concept image for Mixed Weights in Grams, and Back. It follows the idea of changing a weight in kg and g to grams in your maths book and shows the concept's own example (practice values).
images.teaching_notes: Have the student say the g part with its zero place. The slip to watch: writing 40 g in the hundreds place.

image_decisions.why: The three cells show where the 40 g sits, so the zero in the hundreds place is seen.
